_about: Multi-turn journeys. Each turn is labelled with the path it should take GIVEN THE TURNS BEFORE IT, which is the only context in which a fragment like 'is it free?' has a correct answer at all.
_limitation: Written by the same person who wrote the rules, like every other evaluation set in this repo. That makes them a regression harness and a design instrument, not evidence about real girls. The first journey is the one the reviewer described; it was not adjusted afterwards to make anything pass.
_must_not_retrieve: Passages this turn must not be answered from. Not a style rule: a 15-year-old asking a follow-up about the implant and being shown female sterilization is being told about a permanent procedure she did not ask about.

_disputed_labels: Two turns disagree with the router and BOTH labels are mine, written before the run. They are left as written rather than corrected, because changing a label after seeing the result is how an evaluation stops measuring anything. J3 'what will they ask me' -- I labelled factual, the router says access, and the router is arguably right: it is a question about the service encounter. J4 'Can I use family planning if I am not married?' -- I labelled access, the router says factual, and the router is arguably right: it is an eligibility fact, not a question about where to go. Criterion 2 fails at 0.913 because of these two. A reviewer should judge the labels, not just the score.
